option_strategies.name: Long Call
option_strategies.description: Buying a call option to profit from upward price movement. Most basic bullish strategy with limited risk and unlimited profit potential.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately to strongly bullish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk (premium paid), unlimited profit potential
option_strategies.max_profit: Unlimited (Stock Price - Strike Price - Premium Paid)
option_strategies.max_loss: Limited to premium paid
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Strike Price + Premium Paid
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 Call Option at desired strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Roll up to higher strike, convert to bull call spread, take partial profits. Adjustments when losing: Roll down to lower strike, roll out to later expiration, convert to protective put, close position to limit losses.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Buy 1 XYZ 100 Call for $2. Max profit: Unlimited. Max loss: $200. Breakeven: $102.

option_strategies.name: Short Call
option_strategies.description: Selling a call option to collect premium, expecting the stock to stay below the strike price. High probability but limited profit strategy.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to moderately bearish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited profit (premium received), unlimited risk
option_strategies.max_profit: Limited to premium received
option_strategies.max_loss: Unlimited (Strike Price - Stock Price + Premium Received)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Strike Price + Premium Received
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 Call Option at desired strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Buy back call early, roll down to lower strike, let expire worthless. Adjustments when losing: Buy back call to limit losses, roll up and out for credit, convert to covered call, create spread by buying higher strike call.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Sell 1 XYZ 105 Call for $1.50. Max profit: $150. Max loss: Unlimited. Breakeven: $106.50.

option_strategies.name: Long Put
option_strategies.description: Buying a put option to profit from downward price movement. Most basic bearish strategy with limited risk and substantial profit potential.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately to strongly bearish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk (premium paid), substantial profit potential
option_strategies.max_profit: Strike Price - Premium Paid (occurs at stock price = 0)
option_strategies.max_loss: Limited to premium paid
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Strike Price - Premium Paid
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 Put Option at desired strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Roll down to lower strike, convert to bear put spread, take partial profits. Adjustments when losing: Roll up to higher strike, roll out to later expiration, convert to protective call, close position to limit losses.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Buy 1 XYZ 95 Put for $3. Max profit: $9,200 (at $0). Max loss: $300. Breakeven: $92.

option_strategies.name: Short Put
option_strategies.description: Selling a put option to collect premium, expecting the stock to stay above the strike price. Used to generate income or acquire stock at lower price.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to moderately bullish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited profit (premium received), substantial risk
option_strategies.max_profit: Limited to premium received
option_strategies.max_loss: Strike Price - Premium Received (occurs at stock price = 0)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Strike Price - Premium Received
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 Put Option at desired strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Buy back put early, roll up to higher strike, let expire worthless. Adjustments when losing: Buy back put to limit losses, roll down and out for credit, accept assignment if willing to own stock, create spread by buying lower strike put.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Sell 1 XYZ 90 Put for $2. Max profit: $200. Max loss: $8,800 (at $0). Breakeven: $88.

option_strategies.name: Bull Call Spread
option_strategies.description: Buying a lower strike call and selling a higher strike call to profit from moderate upward movement with reduced cost and risk.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bullish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and limited profit
option_strategies.max_profit: Difference in strike prices - net premium paid
option_strategies.max_loss: Net premium paid
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Lower strike price + net premium paid
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 Call (lower strike), Sell 1 Call (higher strike), same expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Close both legs early, roll up both strikes, convert to protective put. Adjustments when losing: Roll out to later expiration, close position to limit losses, convert to ratio spread, let short call expire and manage long call.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Buy XYZ 100 Call for $3, Sell XYZ 105 Call for $1. Net cost: $2. Max profit: $3. Breakeven: $102.

option_strategies.name: Bear Put Spread
option_strategies.description: Buying a higher strike put and selling a lower strike put to profit from moderate downward movement with reduced cost and risk.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bearish
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and limited profit
option_strategies.max_profit: Difference in strike prices - net premium paid
option_strategies.max_loss: Net premium paid
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Higher strike price - net premium paid
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 Put (higher strike), Sell 1 Put (lower strike), same expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Close both legs early, roll down both strikes, convert to protective call. Adjustments when losing: Roll out to later expiration, close position to limit losses, convert to ratio spread, let short put expire and manage long put.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Buy XYZ 95 Put for $4, Sell XYZ 90 Put for $2. Net cost: $2. Max profit: $3. Breakeven: $93.

option_strategies.name: Long Straddle
option_strategies.description: Buying both a call and put at the same strike price, expecting significant price movement in either direction. Pure volatility play.
option_strategies.market_condition: High volatility expected, direction unknown
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk, unlimited profit potential on upside, substantial profit potential on downside
option_strategies.max_profit: Unlimited on upside, substantial on downside (Strike - Premium - Stock Price)
option_strategies.max_loss: Total premium paid for both options
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Upper: Strike + Total Premium; Lower: Strike - Total Premium
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 Call and Buy 1 Put at same strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Take profits on profitable leg, convert to strangle, add butterfly spread. Adjustments when losing: Roll out to later expiration, convert to calendar straddle, convert to iron butterfly, close position if volatility outlook changes.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Buy XYZ 100 Call for $2.50, Buy XYZ 100 Put for $2.50. Total cost: $5. Breakeven: $95 and $105.

option_strategies.name: Short Straddle
option_strategies.description: Selling both a call and put at the same strike price, expecting low volatility and sideways movement to collect premium.
option_strategies.market_condition: Low volatility expected, sideways movement
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited profit, unlimited risk
option_strategies.max_profit: Total premium received from both options
option_strategies.max_loss: Unlimited on both sides (minus premium received)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Upper: Strike + Total Premium; Lower: Strike - Total Premium
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 Call and Sell 1 Put at same strike price and expiration
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Buy back both options early, roll to later expiration, let both expire worthless. Adjustments when losing: Buy back losing side, convert to long straddle, roll entire position out, create iron butterfly.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Sell XYZ 100 Call for $2.50, Sell XYZ 100 Put for $2.50. Total credit: $5. Breakeven: $95 and $105.

option_strategies.name: Iron Condor
option_strategies.description: Combining bull put spread and bear call spread to profit from range-bound movement while collecting premium.
option_strategies.market_condition: Low volatility, range-bound movement expected
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and limited profit, high probability strategy
option_strategies.max_profit: Net credit received when stock stays between short strikes
option_strategies.max_loss: Wing spread width - net credit received
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Lower: Put strike - net credit; Upper: Call strike + net credit
option_strategies.construction: Sell put spread (bull put) + Sell call spread (bear call) with different strikes
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Close early to capture profit, let expire worthless if staying in range, roll out to later expiration. Adjustments when tested: Close threatened side only, convert to iron butterfly, roll entire position out, adjust strikes to follow stock movement.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Sell 95-90 put spread and 105-110 call spread. Profit if XYZ stays between 95-105.

option_strategies.name: Protective Put
option_strategies.description: Buying a put option while owning the underlying stock to protect against downside risk. Portfolio insurance strategy.
option_strategies.market_condition: Bullish long-term but concerned about short-term downside
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited downside risk, unlimited upside potential
option_strategies.max_profit: Unlimited (stock appreciation minus put premium)
option_strategies.max_loss: Stock price - Put strike price + Put premium
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Stock purchase price + Put premium paid
option_strategies.construction: Own 100 shares of stock + Buy 1 Put option
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when stock moves higher: Let put expire worthless, roll put up to higher strike, sell calls against position. Adjustments when stock moves lower: Exercise put to limit losses, roll put down and out, convert to bear put spread, sell covered calls to generate income.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Own 100 XYZ at $102, Buy XYZ 95 Put for $1. Protected below $95, cost $1. Breakeven: $103.

option_strategies.name: Covered Call
option_strategies.description: Selling call options against owned stock to generate income, accepting to sell stock if called away above strike price.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to moderately bullish, income generation
option_strategies.risk_profile: Reduced risk due to income, limited upside potential
option_strategies.max_profit: Strike price - stock cost + premium received
option_strategies.max_loss: Stock cost - premium received (if stock goes to zero)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Stock cost - premium received
option_strategies.construction: Own 100 shares of stock + Sell 1 Call option
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when stock moves higher: Buy back call to keep stock, roll up and out for credit, accept assignment, convert to collar. Adjustments when stock moves lower: Buy back call for profit, let call expire worthless, add protective put, roll call down and out.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Own 100 XYZ at $98, Sell XYZ 105 Call for $2. Max profit: $9 (7+2). Breakeven: $96.

option_strategies.name: Collar
option_strategies.description: Combining protective put and covered call on owned stock to create a risk-defined position with limited profit and loss.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral, seeking protection and income
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and limited profit
option_strategies.max_profit: Call strike - stock cost + net credit (or minus net debit)
option_strategies.max_loss: Stock cost - put strike + net debit (or minus net credit)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Stock cost +/- net debit or credit
option_strategies.construction: Own stock + Buy put (lower strike) + Sell call (higher strike)
option_strategies.adjustments: Adjustments when profitable: Close collar early, roll both strikes up, let call expire and sell new call higher. Adjustments when between strikes: Let both options expire worthless, roll out to later expiration, adjust strikes to new range. Adjustments when threatened: Roll threatened side out, close collar and manage stock separately.
option_strategies.author: George Jabbour & Philip Budwick
option_strategies.examples: Own 100 XYZ at $100, Buy 95 Put for $1, Sell 105 Call for $1.50. Net credit: $0.50.

option_strategies.name: Jade Lizard
option_strategies.description: A bullish/neutral 3-leg strategy combining a short put with a call spread. Designed to have no upside risk when properly constructed.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to slightly bullish, high implied volatility environment
option_strategies.risk_profile: Undefined downside risk, no upside risk when properly constructed, high win rate (70-80%)
option_strategies.max_profit: Net credit received (achieved when stock stays between put strike and call spread strikes)
option_strategies.max_loss: Theoretically unlimited on downside below put strike (mitigate with protective put)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Lower breakeven = Short put strike - net credit received. No upper breakeven due to call spread protection.
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 OTM Put + Sell 1 OTM Call (lower strike) + Buy 1 Further OTM Call (higher strike). Example: Stock at $200 - Sell $190 Put, Sell $210 Call, Buy $220 Call.
option_strategies.adjustments:
If stock rises through call spread: Roll up short put for additional credit to enhance position without added risk.

If stock drops toward short put: Roll down the call spread to collect more credit and mitigate potential losses.

Defensive adjustment: Buy protective put below short put to cap downside risk.

Profit target: Close at 25-50% of maximum profit. Time-based exit: Close with 7-14 days remaining to avoid gamma risk.
option_strategies.author: Various Professional Options Educators
option_strategies.examples: XYZ trading at $50: Sell $45 Put @ $2.50, Sell $52 Call @ $1.50, Buy $57 Call @ $0.50. Net credit: $3.50. Profit if XYZ stays between $41.50-$57. No upside risk beyond $57.

option_strategies.name: Big Lizard
option_strategies.description: A variation of the Jade Lizard where the put and call are sold at the same strike, creating a straddle-like structure with defined upside risk.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral market with expectation of low volatility, high IV environment
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited upside risk, unlimited downside risk, narrower profit zone than Jade Lizard
option_strategies.max_profit: Net credit received when stock closes at short strike at expiration
option_strategies.max_loss: Unlimited on downside, limited on upside by call spread
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Lower breakeven = Short strike - net credit. Upper breakeven = Short strike + net credit.
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 ATM Put + Sell 1 ATM Call + Buy 1 OTM Call (higher strike). Example: Stock at $312 - Sell $312 Put, Sell $312 Call, Buy $329 Call.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Tent-shaped profit zone requires precise management:

If stock moves significantly in either direction: Consider closing entire position early to avoid large losses.

Volatility expansion: May need to close position as short straddle will lose value rapidly.

Time decay management: Most profitable in final weeks before expiration if stock remains near short strike.

Defensive adjustment: Add protective put or call spreads to limit risk on tested side.
option_strategies.author: Professional Options Trading Community
option_strategies.examples: SPY at $312: Sell $312 Put @ $10.22, Sell $312 Call @ $8.57, Buy $329 Call @ $1.84. Net credit: $16.95. Breakeven at $295.05 and $328.95.

option_strategies.name: Iron Butterfly (Advanced)
option_strategies.description: A 4-leg neutral strategy combining a short straddle with protective wings. Profits from minimal price movement and time decay.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral market outlook with low volatility expectations, best in high IV environments
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and reward, high win rate but requires precise price targeting
option_strategies.max_profit: Net credit received when stock closes exactly at middle strike
option_strategies.max_loss: Wing width minus net credit received
option_strategies.breakeven_points: ATM strike ± net credit received
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 ATM Call + Sell 1 ATM Put + Buy 1 OTM Call (higher) + Buy 1 OTM Put (lower). All same expiration.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Position management for tight profit zone:

Early profit taking: Close at 25-50% of maximum profit to avoid gamma risk.

Defensive adjustments: If stock moves toward one wing, consider rolling the untested wing closer for additional credit.

Delta hedging: Buy/sell stock to neutralize directional bias as position moves in/out of money.

Volatility management: Close position if IV drops significantly below entry levels.

Time-based exit: Close 7-14 days before expiration to avoid pin risk.
option_strategies.author: TradeStation & Fidelity Education
option_strategies.examples: XYZ at $200: Sell $200 Call @ $8, Sell $200 Put @ $8, Buy $210 Call @ $3, Buy $190 Put @ $3. Net credit: $10. Max profit if XYZ closes at $200.

option_strategies.name: Reverse Iron Condor
option_strategies.description: A 4-leg strategy designed to profit from large price movements in either direction. Combines bull call spread with bear put spread.
option_strategies.market_condition: Expecting large volatility expansion or significant price movement in either direction
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk (net debit paid), profits from high volatility, requires substantial price movement
option_strategies.max_profit: Strike width minus net debit paid (achieved when stock moves beyond outer strikes)
option_strategies.max_loss: Net debit paid (occurs when stock closes between inner strikes)
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Upper: Long call strike + net debit. Lower: Long put strike - net debit.
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 OTM Put (higher strike) + Sell 1 Further OTM Put (lower) + Buy 1 OTM Call (higher) + Sell 1 Further OTM Call (lower).
option_strategies.adjustments:
Long volatility position management:

Profit taking: Close when achieving 50-75% of maximum profit potential.

Volatility timing: Best entered before earnings or major events when IV is expected to expand.

Time decay enemy: Close position well before expiration if not profitable, as theta works against this strategy.

Adjustment cost consideration: Most adjustments increase cost and risk - often better to close and re-establish.

Directional bias: If stock moves strongly in one direction, consider closing profitable side and letting runner continue.
option_strategies.author: SteadyOptions & TrendSpider
option_strategies.examples: XYZ at $100: Buy $95 Put @ $3, Sell $90 Put @ $1.50, Buy $105 Call @ $3, Sell $110 Call @ $1.50. Net debit: $3. Profit if XYZ moves below $92 or above $108.

option_strategies.name: Call Ratio Backspread
option_strategies.description: A 3-leg bullish strategy with unlimited upside profit potential. Sells 1 call and buys 2 calls at higher strikes.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bullish with expectation of large upward moves, rising implied volatility
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited downside profit, unlimited upside profit, maximum loss between strikes
option_strategies.max_profit: Unlimited above upper breakeven point
option_strategies.max_loss: Occurs between short and long strikes = (Strike difference × 100) - Net credit
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Lower: Net credit (if any). Upper: Short strike + 2 × (Long strike - Short strike) - Net credit.
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 ITM/ATM Call + Buy 2 OTM Calls (higher strike). Typically executed for small credit or debit.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Managing unlimited profit potential:

Optimal timeframe: Enter with 30-60 days to expiration for best time decay differential.

Volatility management: Benefits from IV expansion - consider exiting if IV exceeds 80th percentile.

Profit taking: Close at 75% of expiration cycle or when achieving 200-300% return.

Risk management: If stock stalls between strikes near expiration, close position to avoid maximum loss zone.

Rolling technique: Can roll short strike higher if stock rises early in trade.

Defensive action: Add protective spreads if position moves against you in loss zone.
option_strategies.author: Zerodha Varsity & CME Group
option_strategies.examples: Stock at $50: Sell 1 $50 Call @ $5, Buy 2 $55 Calls @ $2.50 each. Break-even at $0 (credit) and $65. Unlimited profit above $65.

option_strategies.name: Put Ratio Backspread
option_strategies.description: A 3-leg bearish strategy with unlimited downside profit potential. Sells 1 put and buys 2 puts at lower strikes.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bearish with expectation of large downward moves, rising implied volatility
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited upside profit, unlimited downside profit, maximum loss between strikes
option_strategies.max_profit: Unlimited below lower breakeven point as stock approaches zero
option_strategies.max_loss: Occurs between short and long strikes = (Strike difference × 100) - Net credit
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Upper: Net credit (if any). Lower: Short strike - 2 × (Short strike - Long strike) + Net credit.
option_strategies.construction: Sell 1 ITM/ATM Put + Buy 2 OTM Puts (lower strike). Best when executed for net credit.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Bearish backspread management:

Entry timing: Best when IV is low relative to historical levels and expansion expected.

Credit optimization: Aim for net credit entry to eliminate upside risk entirely.

Profit taking: Close position when achieving 200-400% return or at 75% of time to expiration.

Volatility exit: Consider closing if realized volatility exceeds implied volatility significantly.

Risk zone management: Actively monitor position if stock hovers between strikes near expiration.

Adjustment technique: Roll short strike lower if stock drops early in trade cycle.
option_strategies.author: Espresso Trading & Professional Educators
option_strategies.examples: Stock at $100: Sell 1 $100 Put @ $8, Buy 2 $90 Puts @ $3 each. Net credit: $2. Unlimited profit below $78.

option_strategies.name: Broken Wing Butterfly
option_strategies.description: A modified butterfly with unequal strike spacing, eliminating risk on one side while maintaining profit potential.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to slightly directional, high implied volatility environment
option_strategies.risk_profile: Asymmetric risk profile, eliminates risk on one side, 70-80% win rate
option_strategies.max_profit: At the body (middle strike) of the butterfly
option_strategies.max_loss: Limited to net debit paid or small credit risk on broken wing side
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Two breakeven points - calculated based on unequal strike spacing and net premium
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 ITM option + Sell 2 ATM options + Buy 1 OTM option with unequal spacing. Can be structured for credit.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Advanced butterfly management:

High probability setup: Target 12-15% credit of narrow spread width.

Optimal timing: 21 days to expiration (DTE) for rapid time decay.

Profit target: Take profit at 2% of narrowest spread width.

Stop loss: Exit at 2-3x initial credit received.

Delta selection: Start with 32/28/21 delta structure, adjust for 2:1 spread ratio.

Time decay acceleration: Position benefits when underlying stays away from short strikes.

Risk elimination: Broken wing removes risk on one side completely - choose direction based on market bias.
option_strategies.author: Charles Schwab & Interactive Brokers
option_strategies.examples: Put BWB: Buy $155 Put @ $10, Sell 2 $150 Puts @ $7 each, Buy $145 Put @ $5. Net debit: $1. Risk eliminated above $155.

option_strategies.name: Christmas Tree Spread
option_strategies.description: A 6-leg strategy using 1-3-2 configuration across four strikes. Profits from specific price ranges and volatility conditions.
option_strategies.market_condition: Neutral to slightly bullish, high implied volatility expecting collapse
option_strategies.risk_profile: Complex risk profile requiring active management, multiple profit zones
option_strategies.max_profit: Multiple profit zones depending on configuration and underlying movement
option_strategies.max_loss: Limited but varies based on strike selection and market movement
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Multiple breakeven points due to complex 6-leg structure
option_strategies.construction: Buy 1 call at Strike A + Sell 3 calls at Strike C + Buy 2 calls at Strike D. Strikes typically equidistant (e.g., 95-100-105-110).
option_strategies.adjustments:
Complex multi-leg management:

Optimal conditions: Enter during high IV expecting volatility collapse (earnings season).

Precise timing: Requires disciplined entry and exit due to complexity.

Transaction costs: Higher commissions due to 6 legs - factor into profit calculations.

Liquidity requirements: Use highly liquid underlyings to minimize bid-ask spreads.

Position sizing: 1-5 contracts for accounts under $50K due to complexity.

Active monitoring: Multiple legs require constant risk assessment.

Adjustment difficulty: Complex to adjust - often better to close and re-establish.
option_strategies.author: Fidelity & Advanced Trading Educators
option_strategies.examples: Stock at $100: Buy 1 $95 Call, Sell 3 $105 Calls, Buy 2 $115 Calls. Profit zones vary by expiration and volatility.

option_strategies.name: Call Diagonal Spread
option_strategies.description: Uses different strikes AND expiration dates. Combines calendar spread benefits with directional bias.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bullish with specific time decay and volatility expectations
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk and reward, benefits from time decay differential between expirations
option_strategies.max_profit: Time decay differential plus any favorable price movement within range
option_strategies.max_loss: Net debit paid for the spread
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Complex calculation involving time decay, volatility, and price movement
option_strategies.construction: Buy longer-term call (higher strike) + Sell shorter-term call (lower strike). Or buy LEAP call + sell monthly call.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Advanced calendar/diagonal management:

Time decay advantage: Long option decays slower than short option.

Volatility impact: Benefits from IV expansion after short option expires.

Rolling technique: Roll short strikes as they approach expiration.

Stock movement adjustments: If stock rises too high - roll up lower strike for more credit. If stock falls - roll down higher strike.

Poor Mans Covered Call: Buy deep ITM LEAP, sell monthly OTM calls for income.

Exit timing: Close when short option approaches expiration or at profit target.
option_strategies.author: Saxo & Terry's Tips
option_strategies.examples: Buy Jan $105 Call @ $8, Sell Dec $100 Call @ $5. Net debit: $3. Profit from time decay and moderate upward movement.

option_strategies.name: Put Diagonal Spread
option_strategies.description: Bearish diagonal using puts with different strikes and expirations. Profits from downward movement and time decay.
option_strategies.market_condition: Moderately bearish with controlled downward movement expected
option_strategies.risk_profile: Limited risk strategy with defined profit potential from time and price movement
option_strategies.max_profit: Achieved when stock drops to short put strike at near expiration
option_strategies.max_loss: Net debit paid for establishing the position
option_strategies.breakeven_points: Depends on time decay rates and stock price movement between strikes
option_strategies.construction: Buy longer-term put (lower strike) + Sell shorter-term put (higher strike). Creates bearish bias with time advantage.
option_strategies.adjustments:
Bearish diagonal management:

Optimal setup: Short put should be 30-45 days out, long put 60-90 days.

Time decay management: Short put decays faster, creating profit potential.

Movement expectations: Profits from moderate downward movement, not crash scenarios.

Rolling opportunities: Roll short put down and out as it approaches expiration.

Volatility considerations: Benefits from stable or declining implied volatility.

Exit strategies: Close at 50% profit or when short option has 1-2 weeks remaining.
option_strategies.author: Option Alpha & Professional Trading Community
option_strategies.examples: Buy Mar $95 Put @ $6, Sell Feb $100 Put @ $4. Net debit: $2. Profit if stock drops moderately by Feb expiration.
